B13_00: Membrane ruffles are actin-rich folds driven by branched polymerisation, and suppressing them lets a cell limit spreading and migration. ARHGAP24 lowers Rac activity, KANK1 restrains talin-dependent adhesion, ABI3 sits in the WAVE complex without promoting ruffling, and EVL and PFN2 shape filament elongation. This control balances motility against stable contact in epithelial and immune cells and opposes invasive behaviour.
B13_01: This pathway restrains autophagosome formation when nutrients are plentiful, matching self-digestion to demand; too little restraint causes excess sequestration, while too much blocks clearance of damaged mitochondria and aggregates, linked to neurodegeneration via LRRK2 and PINK1. EHMT2 and NUPR1 limit autophagy gene expression, PHF23 restrains BECN1, FEZ1 and FEZ2 hinder assembly, and SEC22B, SCFD1 and TMEM39A control membrane supply.
B13_02: This pathway governs how many inhibitory GABAergic or glycinergic synapses form, setting the excitation-inhibition balance of neural circuits. LHFPL4 clusters gephyrin and GABA-A receptors, calsyntenin-3 and cerebellins engage presynaptic adhesion partners, and semaphorin-plexin signalling tunes contact formation. Reduced inhibitory synapse number is associated with epilepsy and neurodevelopmental disorders with hyperexcitable circuits.
B13_03: Restraints on centriole replication keep each cell to one new centriole per existing one; their loss causes centrosome amplification, multipolar spindles and the aneuploidy typical of tumours. BRCA1 and TRIM37 suppress amplification via ubiquitin ligase activity, CDK5RAP2 organises pericentriolar material, MDM1 and RBM14 block extra cartwheel assembly, and KAT2A and KAT2B limit licensing. Mutations cause microcephalic dwarfism and cancer predisposition.
B13_04: Synaptic vesicle priming sets the size of the readily releasable pool, governing release probability and short-term plasticity; loss causes early-onset epileptic encephalopathies and movement disorders. Syntaxin-1A/B, Munc18-1 and a Munc13 isoform drive SNARE assembly into the primed state, tomosyn restrains it, alpha- and beta-SNAP recycle SNAREs, and synaptophysin, synaptogyrin and a presynaptic kinase add further control.
B13_05: This programme regulates neuromuscular junction assembly where motor neurons meet muscle fibres. Nerve-derived agrin signalling through MuSK clusters acetylcholine receptors, a collagen-tailed subunit anchors acetylcholinesterase in the cleft, SIX factors support muscle differentiation, and scaffolding and ubiquitin-ligase components tune localisation. Loss of agrin-MuSK signalling, or autoantibodies against it, causes congenital myasthenic syndromes and myasthenia gravis.
B13_06: These signals inhibit or dismantle tight junctions, increasing paracellular permeability in epithelia and endothelia; this is normal during wound repair and leukocyte transit but, when sustained, drives leaky gut, blood-brain barrier failure and tumour invasion. TNF and IKK-NF-kB disassemble junctions, ROCK1 and ROCK2 drive actomyosin pulling, and miR-105 and miR-142 repress junction proteins, promoting vascular permeability before metastasis.
B13_07: Capping the pointed end of actin filaments blocks subunit exchange there and fixes filament length. Tropomodulins cap minus ends together with tropomyosin, while related leiomodins nucleate filaments and compete for the site, jointly setting thin filament length in muscle and stabilising erythrocyte and neuronal actin. LMOD3 loss causes nemaline myopathy and TMOD1 loss disrupts myofibril assembly.
B13_08: Proteins that cap actin barbed ends determine whether networks grow, and regulating this capping tunes lamellipodial protrusion, migration and cortical remodelling in adhesion and immunity. CARMIL proteins lower capping protein affinity to allow uncapping, myotrophin antagonises capping protein, a WASH subunit links capping to endosomal nucleation, and cofilin creates new ends by severing. CARMIL2 deficiency impairs T cell activation.
B13_09: Restraining lamellipodium assembly lets migrating cells stop, turn or remain still, shaping axon guidance, wound repair, angiogenesis and tumour invasion. Cofilin turns over actin, an ABI family member dampens WAVE-Arp2/3 nucleation, plexin and Slit receptors collapse protrusions by reducing Rac activity, histidine-rich glycoprotein acts extracellularly, and two microRNAs tune output. Loss yields persistent, poorly directed motility.
B13_10: These signals tune assembly of the postsynaptic specialization, controlling dendritic spine number, shape and synaptic strength; defects contribute to intellectual disability, autism and schizophrenia. Rho-family signalling via Rac1, Rac3, DOCK activators, ARHGAP inactivators, RhoG and GNA13 remodels spine actin, adhesion receptors such as neurexin and LRP4 position contacts, and neddylation, retromer, CPEB3 and PUM2 supply components.
B13_11: This pathway restrains filopodia formation, limiting how many protrusions cells and growth cones produce. In neurons it paces spine maturation and synapse formation, and human-specific SRGAP2C antagonises SRGAP2, linked to prolonged spine development in human cortex. Rho GTPase regulation, membrane deformation and traffic, kinase signalling and neurexin-1 also contribute, and loss causes excess protrusions and miswiring.
B13_12: Brakes on NLRP3 inflammasome assembly prevent excessive caspase-1 activation, IL-1β and IL-18 release and pyroptosis; their loss underlies periodic fever syndromes and contributes to gout, atherosclerosis and neuroinflammation. TRIM31 and FBXL2 degrade NLRP3, IRGM and LAMP2-dependent autophagy clear it, PYDC1 and PYDC2 act as decoys, and depalmitoylases, kinases, SIRT2 and TREM2 tune its activity.
B13_13: This pathway suppresses tubulin polymerisation and limits plus-end growth, setting microtubule length and turnover so spindles and growth cones can remodel. Stathmins sequester tubulin and promote catastrophe, STMN2 acting in axons; MAPRE1, MAP2 and tubulin cofactors shape the polymer, and DYRK1A and stathmin phosphorylation link it to signalling. Loss contributes to axonal degeneration, and alpha-synuclein links it to synucleinopathy.
B13_14: These signals restrain synapse formation, refining developing circuits and limiting excitatory drive; loss is associated with excess spines, aberrant connectivity and epileptiform activity. Wnt ligands and DKK1 suppress synapses, Slit-Robo and Eph receptors deliver repulsive cues, cerebellin and calsyntenin can curb assembly, and TLR2 signalling and NEGR1 modulate neurite and synapse number, contributing to pruning.
B13_15: This pathway controls SNARE complex assembly, setting where and when membranes fuse. In neurons STXBP1 chaperones syntaxin-1 for vesicle priming and its loss causes infantile epilepsy, PRRT2 mutations cause paroxysmal dyskinesia, and alpha-synuclein affects SNARE formation. In the endolysosomal system HOPS and CORVET subunits couple tethering to SNARE engagement, while LRRK2 and STXBP6 modulate assembly.
B13_16: Under oxidative, heat or nutrient stress, stalled translation complexes condense into stress granules, sequestering mRNA and supporting survival; aberrant condensation can seed neurodegenerative aggregation. UBAP2L, CAPRIN1 and IGF2BP1 promote granule formation, USP10 with G3BP scaffolds restrains it, AMPK catalytic subunits couple it to energy stress, and ATG5 and BECN1 link granule clearance to autophagy.
B13_17: This pathway controls whether and how fast proteins assemble into dimers and larger complexes, which matters because the same chemistry can produce pathological aggregates when quality control fails. Regulators include an acetyltransferase coactivator and a cytoplasmic deacetylase involved in aggresome clearance, an oxygenase, ISG15 conjugation, a TRIM ubiquitin ligase, and VPS35-dependent retromer sorting of membrane cargo.
B13_18: Cytosolic double-stranded DNA from microbes or damaged nuclei triggers AIM2 inflammasome assembly, leading to caspase-1 activation, IL-1β and IL-18 maturation and pyroptosis, and mistuning contributes to autoinflammation. Guanylate-binding proteins lyse vacuoles and bacteria to release DNA, IFI16 is a related DNA sensor, pyrin-only decoy proteins block PYD polymerisation, and TRIM11 adds ubiquitin-dependent control.
B13_19: These processes tune how quickly and accurately the bipolar mitotic spindle forms; errors cause multipolar spindles, lagging chromosomes and aneuploidy, and some members are drug targets. ESCRT-III CHMP proteins with VPS4B and ALIX link membrane remodelling to spindle organisation, PLK1 provides kinase control, RCC1 generates the RanGTP gradient, CEP97 restrains centrioles, and EML3 and HNRNPU stabilise spindle microtubules.
